issuing_body: European Commission (AI Office) / General-Purpose AI Code of Practice Working Group 1
covered_actors: Providers of fine-tuned or modified general-purpose AI models

evidence.quote: Signatories, when placing a general-purpose AI model on the market, will have documented at least all the information referred to in the Model Documentation Form below (hereafter this information is referred to as the ‘Model Documentation’).

Signatories will update the Model Documentation to reflect relevant changes in the information contained in the Model Documentation, including in relation to updated versions of the same model, while keeping previous versions of the Model Documentation for a period ending 10 years after the model has been placed on the market.

In accordance with Article 53(2) AI Act, these Measures do not apply to providers of general-purpose AI models released under a free and open-source license that satisfy the conditions specified in that provision, unless the model is a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk.

Some of this information may also be required in a summarised form as part of the training content summary that providers must make publicly available under Article 53(1), point (d), AI Act, according to a template to be provided by the AI Office.

To ensure providers of general-purpose AI models comply with their obligations under the AI Act and to enable the AI Office to assess compliance of providers of general-purpose AI models who choose to rely on the Code to demonstrate compliance with their obligations under the AI Act.

Information intended for the AI Office or national competent authorities is only to be made available following a request from the AI Office, either ex officio or based on a request to the AI Office from national competent authorities.

Signatories will provide, upon a request from the AI Office pursuant to Articles 91 or 75(3) AI Act for one or more elements of the Model Documentation, or any additional information, that are necessary for the AI Office to fulfil its tasks under the AI Act or for national competent authorities to exercise their supervisory tasks under the AI Act

To serve as a guiding document for demonstrating compliance with the obligations provided for in Articles 53 and 55 AI Act, while recognising that adherence to the Code does not constitute conclusive evidence of compliance with these obligations under the AI Act.
Signatories are encouraged to consider whether the documented information can be disclosed, in whole or in part, to the public to promote public transparency.

compliance_deadlines: Document Model Documentation and publicly disclose contact information when placing a general-purpose AI model on the market
Retain previous versions of Model Documentation for 10 years after the model has been placed on the market
Provide requested information to the AI Office within the period specified in the AI Office's request under Article 91(4) AI Act
Provide requested additional information to downstream providers within a reasonable timeframe and no later than 14 days of receiving the request, save for exceptional circumstances
implementation_notes: This Transparency Chapter of the EU GPAI Code of Practice sets out three voluntary Measures (1.1–1.3) and a Model Documentation Form to help Signatories demonstrate compliance with Article 53(1)(a)–(b) and Annexes XI (Section 1) and XII of the EU AI Act, though adherence does not constitute conclusive evidence of compliance. Free and open-source GPAI models satisfying Article 53(2) AI Act are exempt unless they are GPAI models with systemic risk; systemic-risk documentation under Annex XI Section 2 is addressed separately in Measure 10.1 of the Safety and Security Chapter. Information for the AI Office or national competent authorities is provided only upon formal request, and recipients must uphold confidentiality and cybersecurity safeguards under Articles 53(7) and 78 AI Act.
